title: The Man and the Lion
summary: A man and a lion were traveling together down a highway, debating which of their kinds possessed superior strength, nobility, and courage....
full_text:
A man and a lion were traveling together down a highway, debating which of their kinds possessed superior strength, nobility, and courage.

As they entered a public square in a grand city, the man pointed triumphantly to a colossal marble statue depicting a heroic huntsman standing victorious over a slain lion, pinning the beast beneath his heel.

"See there!" exclaimed the man in boasting pride. "Look at that monument! Does that not prove beyond dispute that man is mightier than the lion?"

The lion smiled calmly, flicked his tail, and replied:

"If lions knew how to carve stone statues as men do, friend, you would see a hundred monuments showing one lion tearing ten huntsmen to shreds!"
moral: History is written by the narrator; perspective changes when both sides tell the tale.
